clue.text: Tree-dwelling, headless snake climbs — true!

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters run upwards, so read the trimmed snake backwards
the snake loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: a cobra is a venomous snake
true means real

explanation.surface: An excited remark that a snake really does climb trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' takes C off COBRA, leaving OBRA, and 'climbs' turns that upwards to ARBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreal is the zoologist's adjective for animals that live in trees.

clue.text: Paid less — lacking pass, not working

indicators.note: lacking says the letters of the next word are removed from the phrase before it

parts.note: taken as written; the four left-over letters are what the deletion leaves, a coincidence rather than a hidden word
the four letters of pass are struck out one by one, in order

explanation.surface: Someone paid less after missing a pass, so off work.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P, A, S, S from PAIDLESS in order and IDLE is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle is a plain synonym for unemployed or inactive, describing a person or machine at rest.

clue.text: Listlessness can make one reject help

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the help word is turned round

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A claim that apathy can make a person refuse assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' as ACE is the card convention; 'can make' is only the link between definition and wordplay, though it reads as part of the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Acedia is an old word for spiritual sloth and apathy, the medieval monk's torpor.

clue.text: Setter is in a blessed state, despite expression

indicators.note: the setter's words are placed inside the blessed state

parts.note: being in a state of grace is being blessed by God
the setter speaks of himself as I, and 'setter is' gives I'M

explanation.surface: A setter claims to be in a state of grace whatever his face shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter is' means I am, the setter referring to himself; 'despite' is only a loose link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial look of pain or disgust, a kind of facial expression.

clue.text: Flower not entirely like the Taoiseach

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: the Taoiseach is the prime minister of Ireland, so he is Irish

explanation.surface: A flower that is only somewhat like the Irish prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a garden flower with sword-shaped leaves, named for the rainbow goddess.

clue.text: Hector's wife had Cameron shattered

indicators.note: shattered means broken in pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hector's wife had David Cameron worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' looks like a British word for exhausted describing Cameron, but it signals the anagram of HADCAMERON.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Iliad the Trojan hero Hector is married to Andromache.

clue.text: Item in service reported to decrease

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word that is said is a sound-alike

parts.note: to lessen is to decrease

explanation.surface: Something in a church service is said to be getting smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a Bible reading in a church service, read by a member of the congregation.

clue.text: Director blows up record

indicators.note: blows up suggests an explosion; here blows alone signals the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A film director inflates a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows up' looks like one verb, but 'blows' is the anagram signal and 'up' is fodder with RECORD.
explanation.definitionFit: A producer, like a director, is the one in charge of making a film or play.

clue.text: Get up about noon for a quick dip

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: Getting up around midday for a fast swim.
explanation.definitionFit: A rinse is a brief wash or dunk in water, a quick soaking.

clue.text: Schools' governor? Not half!

indicators.note: a British exclamation meaning very much, but read literally it says only half the word is taken

explanation.surface: Asked whether someone runs the schools, the answer is a hearty yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove was Britain's Education Secretary, so in charge of schools. 'Not half!' is British slang for 'absolutely', but takes the first half of GOVERNOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Gove ran English schools as Education Secretary from 2010 to 2014.

clue.text: Plant that makes roads collapse

indicators.note: collapse means fall to pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant whose roots wreck road surfaces.
explanation.definitionFit: The damask rose is a fragrant shrub rose, a garden plant used for rose oil.

clue.text: Foreigners express gratitude with a chunk of Olde England

parts.note: merci is what the French say for thanks

explanation.surface: Foreign visitors give thanks for a slice of old England.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercia was one of the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms, covering the English Midlands.

clue.text: One with the opportunity to turn round?

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word for turn is written backwards

parts.note: to roll is to turn over

explanation.surface: Someone given a chance to turn things round.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints at the semi-literal reading: a chancellor, of the Exchequer, has the chance to turn the economy round.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancellor is a person in high office, so one such individual fits the bare definition.

clue.text: "Roger", as in building material

indicators.note: in places the small word inside the building material

parts.note: cement is a building material

explanation.surface: A radio operator says roger, as if laying building material.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger Casement was an Irish nationalist executed for treason in 1916; 'Roger' looks like radio slang for 'understood'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Roger Casement was a British diplomat turned Irish rebel, hanged in 1916.

clue.text: Source of water in outer space?

indicators.note: in says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asking whether water might be found out among the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a mineral spring, a natural source of healing water.

clue.text: Billingsgate titfer held plate for fish

indicators.note: held says one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: titfer is rhyming slang (tit for tat) for hat; a straw boater suits London's Billingsgate fish market
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A fish-market porter's hat held a plate of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Billingsgate is London's fish market; titfer is Cockney rhyming slang for a hat, here the flat straw boater. L for 'plate' is the L-plate a British learner driver displays.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloater is a whole herring that is salted and smoked.

clue.text: The "old days" are over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: The good old days are finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a period of history, such as times gone by.

clue.text: Some science in firm grip of an extremist

indicators.note: in places some of the science inside the firm grip

parts.note: something held in a firm grip is held fast
SCI, the first three letters, is some of the word science, also its usual short form

explanation.surface: Some science held tightly by a political extremist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm grip' suggests a handshake; here it is FAST, as in held fast, gripping the science.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascist is a follower of an authoritarian far-right ideology, a political extremist.

clue.text: Put by for Jack abroad

parts.note: Jack, like salt, is a nickname for a sailor
abroad means away from home

explanation.surface: Savings set aside for a sailor overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To salt away money is to save it, putting it by for later.

clue.text: Reptiles, not soft but awkwardly unproductive

indicators.note: awkwardly means clumsily arranged, so the remaining letters are mixed up
not says a letter is left out of the reptiles

parts.note: p is piano, the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Reptiles that are hard rather than soft and fail to breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not soft' removes P from REPTILES, leaving RETILES, which 'awkwardly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile describes an animal or land that is barren, unable to produce offspring or crops.

clue.text: Commercial sea song?

parts.note: mer is French for sea
a chant is a song

explanation.surface: A sea shanty used as an advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial' looks like a noun for an advertisement but is the adjective, as in merchant shipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchant as an adjective means trading or commercial, as in merchant bank or merchant navy.

clue.text: Little time before surrounding an animal

indicators.note: surrounding says the word for before goes round the short time

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
min is short for minute, a little time

explanation.surface: A brief moment before encircling a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An ermine is a stoat in its white winter coat, a small mammal.

clue.text: English wearing a winning medal is nothing new

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the medal goes round the English letter

parts.note: gold is the winner's medal

explanation.surface: An English athlete in a gold medal is old news.
explanation.definitionFit: Age-old describes something that has existed for a very long time, the opposite of fresh.

clue.text: In a book about the beginning of history

indicators.note: about means around, so the book goes round the initial letter

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A book covering the dawn of history.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at home is to be in, present at one's house.

clue.text: College enough for a little theology

parts.note: ample means plenty, enough
TH, the opening pair, is a little of the word theology

explanation.surface: A college with enough on offer for some religious study.
explanation.walkthrough: Ampleforth is a Benedictine Catholic boarding school in Yorkshire, England, a fitting place for theology.
explanation.definitionFit: Ampleforth College is a well-known Catholic independent school in North Yorkshire.

clue.text: Hired a straight man

definitions.meaning: paid a fee to, engaged for a charge
the comic's stooge who sets up the jokes

explanation.definitionFit: Fee'd means paid a fee, so hired; a comedian's feed is the partner who supplies cues for punchlines.

clue.text: Vehicle turns over, but not altogether

indicators.note: turns over means the letters are flipped backwards

parts.note: part means not wholly, not altogether

explanation.surface: A vehicle flips, but only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a light two-wheeled carriage drawn by a horse.

clue.text: Check acceptable but proscribed

parts.note: a tab is a bill, a check in American English
U means upper-class and so socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A bill that is acceptable but banned.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, meaning forbidden.

clue.text: Ulster order was turned to stone

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
the OBE is the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: An Ulster honour that petrified someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Niobe, in Greek myth, wept for her slain children until she was turned to stone; the definition describes her.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the grieving mother Niobe was changed into a weeping rock.

clue.text: One man able to produce a legume

indicators.note: to produce suggests making something new out of the given letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single capable man growing a bean.
explanation.definitionFit: The lima bean is a flat pale bean, a legume of the pea family.
